title: Merging two slug functions that drifted apart
measures: Does a behavior-preserving dedupe of two slug implementations that look like copies but differ: product handles keep underscores (\W vs [^a-z0-9]) and are trimmed before the cut (so a cut can leave a trailing dash), posts are cut at 80 and then trimmed. A shared function written from one copy with only the length as a parameter passes the visible tests but changes the URLs new products and posts get.
prompt: src/blog/posts.js and src/shop/products.js each have their own copy of the slug code. Please move it into one shared slugify in src/lib/slug.js and use it from both. It's a pure refactor: posts and products must keep getting exactly the same slugs and handles as today.

commits.message: feat(blog): posts with slugs; products with url handles
